test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 10 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: 3 years ago from now, the age of father was 14 years more than twice his son's age. After how many years, from now, will he be twice his son's age?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **son's age 3 years ago** be **x**.

**Father's age 3 years ago** = 2x + 14.

Difference between their ages = (2x + 14) − x = **x + 14**.

The **age difference** remains constant; when the father is twice the son's age, the son's age must equal the difference (x + 14).

Future age of son = x + 14. Present age of son = x + 3.

Years from now = (x + 14) − (x + 3) = 11 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 11 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a1610c8712278337dd195713e70c0a2fed7c9b196b07c6102a78e304d54f692.png] 

**Given:**

Let the **present age** of **father** be **F** and **son** be **S**.

**Calculations:**

⇒ 3 years ago: (F − 3) = 2(S − 3) + 14

⇒ F − 3 = 2S − 6 + 14

⇒ F − 2S = 11 ...........(i)

Let the father be twice his son's age after **n** years from now.

⇒ (F + n) = 2(S + n)

⇒ F + n = 2S + 2n

⇒ F − 2S = n ...........(ii)

Equating (i) and (ii):

⇒ n = 11

**∴ The correct answer is 11 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two people remains **constant** regardless of the number of years that pass.

Ratio of Ages

If the ratio of ages is given for two different time periods, use the **cross-multiplication** method or equate the difference in ratio units.

Twice Age Rule

When person A is twice the age of person B, the age of person B at that moment is exactly equal to the **difference in their ages**.</p
